items.title: Touted as Waze alternative, TuJu now redirects users to Google Maps
items.summary: New Straits Times KUALA LUMPUR: TuJu users are now being redirected to Google Maps when they tap the navigation button. This comes following the app's latest update amid efforts to resolve navigation disruptions. The Android update, version 2.0.4, released on Oct 30, replaces TuJu's in-app navigation with Google Maps.

items.title: Private universities steal the spotlight as Malaysia sets a historic record in QS Asia 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — More than 50 Malaysian universities penetrated the QS World University Rankings Asia 2027 for the first time, with 11 emerging among the top 100 in Asia. They include Sunway University, INTI International University, Asia Pacific University of Technology and Innovation (APU), SEGi University, IMU University, MILA University, Tunku Abdul Rahman University of Management and Technology, Perdana University, Quest International University (QIU), Nilai University, UNITAR International University and Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Sultan Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah (UniSHAMS). Sunway University also ranked among the top 50 for the first time while INTI International University made it into the top 100 for the first time.

items.title: Status won't protect domestic violence perpetrators, says Penang exco member
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A person's social status, background or public standing will not protect him or her from action against domestic violence. Social Development, Welfare and Non-Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Lim Siew Khim said no one was above the law. "Domestic violence does not discriminate based on position, title, or social status.

items.title: Hafidz Othman appointed new Prisons Department chief, takes office on Nov 5
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 3 — Deputy Commissioner General of Prisons (Community) Hafidz Othman has been appointed the new Commissioner General of Prisons, effective Nov 5, the Prisons Department said. In a statement today, the department said Hafidz received his appointment letter from Public Service director-general Tan Sri Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz. He also served as Deputy Commissioner General of Prisons (Management) in 2025.

items.title: Jais tracking owners of Puchong warehouse in 6.5-tonne halal chicken probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Selangor Islamic Religious Affairs Department (Jais) is tracking down the owners of a Puchong warehouse where more than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken were seized over halal violations. Jais' investigations found that the premises had no proper signage, halal certification application records or a Halal Certification Certificate. Shahzihan said the Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) had never issued slaughterer certification for activities at the site.

items.title: Govt pays RM20.27b in income tax refunds to 3.65m taxpayer cases as at Oct 31
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — A total of RM20.271 billion in income tax refunds involving 3.65 million taxpayer cases had been paid as at Oct 31, 2026. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said of the total, RM6.84 billion had been refunded to 3.4 million individual taxpayers, while RM13.036 billion had been refunded to 206,234 corporate taxpayers, including micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Amir Hamzah reiterated the government’s commitment to addressing the backlog of excess income tax refunds to ensure that all outstanding payments are made promptly.

items.title: Najib fundraising drive still short of target, says Umno sec-gen
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Public donations to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak continue to come in, although the fundraising drive has yet to reach its target to cover his fine. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said daily collections averaged between RM5,000 and RM10,000. Also present were BN candidate for the Durian Tunggal seat Datuk Dr Mustafa Musa and former assemblyman Datuk Zahari Khalil.

items.title: Rayer: Why hasn't Zakir Naik been extradited, who pays for apartment, bodyguards?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong) has questioned why the government will not extradite preacher Dr Zakir Naik to India. Does the government bear the cost?" He said the government had not received any new extradition request from India concerning Zakir.

items.title: SP Setia unit, Help seal deal for Kinrara International School
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: SP Setia Bhd's unit Perumahan Kinrara Bhd and Help Kinrara Sdn Bhd have signed a build-and-lease agreement for a new international school in Bandar Kinrara. SP Setia will develop the purpose-built campus, and Help will lease and operate it as the fourth school in the group, targeted to open in August 2029. The international school will be developed on a 0.81-hectare site within the 6.45-hectare commercial land parcel in Bandar Kinrara.

items.title: Civil society groups demand cross-party deal on eight key reforms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A coalition of civil society organisations (CSOs) wants the government and opposition to sign a cross-party agreement involving all 218 members of parliament. This, they said, was to execute eight key institutional reforms before the end of the 15th Parliament's term. They said that without such an agreement, key reforms may be held back by political uncertainties and may be susceptible to unelected forces that do not want these reforms to empower Malaysian voters.

items.title: TNB accelerates grid modernisation to meet rising current, future demand: CEO
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) is stepping up investments in grid infrastructure and accelerating network modernisation to strengthen Malaysia's electricity supply system, enhance renewable energy integration and meet future demand. Speaking during the "The Grid of Tomorrow" panel at Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW) 2026, he said TNB was investing ahead of demand while balancing the need for affordable, sustainable and reliable electricity supply. Meanwhile, the Santong BESS, which commenced operations in April 2026, is Malaysia's first grid-connected battery energy storage system.

items.title: Johor identifies 337 flood hotspots as state braces for northeast monsoon
items.summary: He said the relevant projects included Phase 1 of the Sungai Johor Flood Mitigation Plan, the Sungai Pemandi Flood Mitigation Plan and a flood alleviation project in Kampung Sungai Kapal Lama in Pengerang. In Batu Pahat, Mohamad Fazli said the DID had identified 41 flood hotspots, while the JKR had detected 21 high-risk locations along federal and state roads, covering a total distance of 6.5 kilometres. In Segamat, Mohamad Fazli said the DID had identified 29 flood hotspots, while the JKR had identified 16 high-risk locations, comprising eight federal roads and eight state roads.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN-PN cooperation goes beyond paper, machinery work together
items.summary: Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the development was a good sign for BN and its candidates. He said this was evident in Melaka, where BN and PN campaign machinery had been attending campaign programmes together, particularly night ceramah. "PN machinery has been helping in areas contested by BN, while BN machinery has also been instructed to give full support in areas contested by PN.

items.title: After Customs flags import irregularities, maritime expert asks MACC to revisit RM220m crude cargo report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — A maritime industry executive today asked whether the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) would take further action on his report over alleged discrepancies in petroleum cargo records, following the Royal Malaysian Customs Department’s latest disclosure on import declaration irregularities. Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan lodged the report on June 5 over alleged discrepancies between bills of lading and the physical movement of petroleum cargo at Tanjung Langsat Port, Johor, in transactions reportedly worth millions of ringgit. Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of experience in the maritime industry, questioned whether the latest information from Customs could give MACC grounds to revisit the concerns raised in his report.

items.title: Proton closes in on 200,000-unit sales milestone
items.summary: Proton sold 21,624 units in October, its second-highest monthly sales performance this year and the strongest start to the fourth quarter since 2005. Year-to-date (YTD) sales rose 40.5 per cent year-on-year, giving Proton an estimated market share of 27.1 per cent. Proton S70 recorded 3,029 units in October, its second-best monthly performance this year, taking YTD sales to 23,448 units, up 63.5 per cent.

items.title: Tanker-car crash shuts all southbound NSE lanes, triggers 7km traffic jam
items.summary: KLUANG: Traffic on the North-South Expressway came to a standstill following a collision involving a tanker lorry and a car at Km50.4, southbound, today. Plus Info Traffic confirmed that all lanes closed following the 5.03pm accident, which caused traffic to back up for 7km. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM NOV 3, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed higher on Tuesday as global investors repositioned towards emerging markets ahead of the US midterm elections. The key index rose more than two points to 1,621 at the closing bell. JW8W_UklIcE © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: IOI Corp, TNB unit team up for 500MW solar project in Bahau
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IOI Corp Bhd's wholly owned Luminous Aspect Sdn Bhd has partnered with Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) subsidiary to develop a 500-megawatt (MW) solar project in Negri Sembilan. The project marks IOI's first large-scale renewable energy development under the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme. TRe will hold a 70 per cent stake in Bahau Energy Ventures Sdn Bhd, the renewable energy development company.

items.title: Govt has settled RM20.71bil in tax refunds as of Oct 31
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has refunded RM20.71 billion in excess tax payments involving 3.65 million taxpayers as of Oct 31. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said RM6.84 billion of the total was refunded to 3.4 million individual taxpayers. Meanwhile, Amir Hamzah said unclaimed money stood at RM14 billion as at Sept 30.

items.title: New law replacing AUKU will not curtail students’ freedom of expression, says Zahid
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 3 — The new Bill to replace the now-repealed Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) will not affect students’ freedom of expression, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. He said the Cabinet agreed that the proposed legislation would be limited to matters concerning university administration, including academic affairs, governance and the appointment of senate members, Ahmad Zahid also said that the new law would also cover the selection of university management personnel, including vice-chancellors and deputy vice-chancellors. “Under AUKU, universities did take action against students.

items.title: Global oil price volatility: Govt sticking to targeted subsidies to protect Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is maintaining its RM40 billion fuel subsidy commitment under the 2027 Budget to shield Malaysians from global oil price volatility and curb subsidy leakages. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the government remained committed to targeted subsidies to protect the people from rising global prices while ensuring that assistance reached the intended beneficiaries. Amir Hamzah said, through Budi Madani, Malaysians continued to enjoy subsidised RON95 petrol of up to 300 litres at RM1.99 per litre, compared with the actual market price of RM4.42 per litre.

items.title: UiTM to enrol first batch of Quantum Technology students next year
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) is expected to enrol its first batch of students in Quantum Technology next year. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said a Department of Quantum Technology would first be established to prepare the country for developments in the field. "We will establish the department first.

items.title: Govt approves over RM250m for ECRL expansion plans and new Kota Bharu bus terminal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 3 — The Madani government has approved more than RM250 million to strengthen the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) development in Kelantan, according to the Ministry of Finance (MOF). This includes building a new bus terminal at the Kota Bharu ECRL Station and preliminary works for a proposed extension to Rantau Panjang, said the ministry in a statement today. Of the total, RM30 million has been allocated for the new bus terminal, while more than RM200 million will fund preliminary works for the proposed ECRL extension from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang.

items.title: Smoke from faulty air-conditioner triggers alarm at Johor hospital's pathology lab
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A faulty air-conditioning unit triggered a smoke scare at the Sultanah Aminah Hospital' s pathology laboratory here today. Fire and Rescue Department operation commander Amirudin Mohamad said 12 firefighters from the Larkin station arrived at 4.07pm, eight minutes after the emergency call was placed. Checks on the fourth floor of the building traced the smoke to damaged equipment inside an air-handling unit (AHU) room.

items.title: Fashion Valet trial: Investment funds cannot be used to pay dividends, court told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Sessions Court hearing the case involving Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd (Fashion Valet) founders Datin Vivy Sofinas Yusof and her husband, Datuk Fadzarudin Shah Anuar, was told today that investment funds could not be used to pay dividends to any party, including the company’s shareholders. Corporate lawyer Anne Wong Wai Yee, 49, who was involved in drafting the shareholders’ agreement between the couple and seven other companies, including Fashion Valet, on March 5, 2018, said the agreement did not contain any provision allowing investment funds to be used for such payments. Capital Sdn Bhd, Transasia E-Commerce Inc., Start Today Co. Ltd., Reussi Sdn Bhd and Pulau Tiga Ventures Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Cooperative manager pleads guilty to cheating by using fake documents for loan
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A cooperative manager pleaded guilty at the Sessions court here today to cheating a man with false supporting documents for a personal financing application four years ago. She was accused of dishonestly inducing Ibrahim Ali, 61, to believe that details in supporting documents submitted for the financing application were genuine, when they allegedly contained false information. Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission prosecuting officer Fazal Lisam Abidin proposed bail of RM10,000 with one local surety pending the next court date.

items.title: Students' political views should be welcomed, as long as 3R is not involved
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Universities should not take disciplinary action against students for holding differing political views and beliefs, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. Apart from that, universities should not take disciplinary action against students simply because they hold differing opinions and political beliefs," he said. However, he stressed that students would remain subject to the country's laws, including criminal laws.

items.title: Ringgit eases against greenback amid AI investment pullback
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit eased against the US dollar on Tuesday amid a pullback in global artificial intelligence (AI)-related trades and investments. SPI Asset Management managing partner Stephen Innes said the ringgit's weakness was largely driven by broader risk aversion, particularly as investors unwound AI-related investments. When investors start pulling back from the AI trade, the ringgit can come under pressure even when the broader US dollar is weakening.

items.title: Bridging rural digital skills gap with AI, digital training
items.summary: The digital skills gap remains evident between rural and urban communities. A community-based initiative launched on Oct 28 aims to address this gap by equipping residents with essential digital skills before introducing them to AI, programming and game development. [[nid:1569976]] Funded by Microsoft, the programme aims to improve digital and AI literacy among local communities, including entrepreneurs who want to use technology to improve their businesses.

items.title: Yinson GreenTech taps carbon credit market via Saxon Renewables pact
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Yinson GreenTech has partnered with Saxon Renewables to generate verified carbon credits from eligible electric vehicle (EV) activities. The carbon programme is registered under Verra's Verified Carbon Standard (VCS). The partnership is the first technology-based carbon project advanced under Yinson's Carbon Project Framework.

items.title: FashionValet investment funds cannot be used to pay dividends, court told [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Investment funds channelled into FashionValet Sdn Bhd could not be used to pay dividends to any party, including the company's shareholders, the Sessions Court heard today. The six companies were Proven Holding Sdn Bhd, My E.G. Capital Sdn Bhd, Transasia E-Commerce Inc., Start Today Co. Ltd., Reussi Sdn Bhd and Pulau Tiga Ventures Sdn Bhd.

items.title: RHB partners MEOA to boost plantation productivity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Bank Bhd has partnered with the Malaysian Estate Owners' Association (MEOA) to promote sustainable investment and improve productivity in the plantation sector. The two-year partnership will provide financing solutions, industry engagement and technical support to help plantation operators adopt sustainable practices and strengthen business resilience. RHB group chief sustainability officer Angus Salim Amran said closer cooperation between financial institutions and industry players was needed to accelerate the sector's sustainability transition.

items.title: Traders risk RM100,000 fine for hidden charges, Parliament told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Traders who impose hidden charges or disclose additional fees only at the final stage of a transaction may face legal action, including fines of up to RM100,000, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. He said the practice misled consumers and undermined their right to know the actual price before making a purchase. Armizan said Section 10B(1) of the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011 [Act 723] allows action against businesses that fail to include all taxes, duties, and other charges in the prices of goods or services they display, advertise, publish, or quote.

items.title: UK PM to raise debt reset and trade at Commonwealth summit
items.summary: ST JOHN'S: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will set out his vision for a debt reset and stronger trade with Commonwealth countries at a summit on Tuesday that is likely to hear calls for slavery reparations. Burnham will join King Charles and leaders from the Commonwealth's 56 member states in Antigua and Barbuda, where he will argue that the organisation can play a bigger role in tackling global challenges including climate change, economic growth and security. But Burnham said at the weekend he was open to calls for a formal apology for Britain's historical role in slavery, although not the payment of reparations.

items.title: GWM WEY G9 hybrid: Luxury without the plug
items.summary: THE self-charging hybrid brings a more accessible entry point to GWM's premium MPV range, pairing all-wheel drive with a cabin designed around passenger comfort. The recent climb towards Genting Highlands provided an appropriate setting to put the GWM WEY G9 Hi4 HEV through its paces, with the media drive taking in trunk roads and a stretch of Karak Highway before returning to Genting Awana. Hybrid Power, Without Charging Stops Priced at RM249,800, the WEY G9 Hi4 HEV is RM20,000 cheaper than its plug-in hybrid (PHEV) sibling.

items.title: Khazanah Wolfson Press Fellows mentor next generation of communicators
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) communications students were given an insight into newsroom operations today, thanks to four Khazanah Wolfson Press Fellows. The Khazanah Residency Programme (KRP) "POV: Your Work in Comms", was hosted by IIUM's Department of Communication, Abdul Hamid Abu Sulayman Kulliyyah of Islamic Revealed Knowledge and Human Sciences (AHAS KIRKHS), with more than 70 students from the department taking part. AHAS KIRHS dean Professor Dr Hafiz Zakariya thanked Khazanah Nasional Bhd for choosing the department for the programme, saying the engagement with industry practitioners allowed students to understand how academic knowledge is applied in the real world.

items.title: The Great Gap: Why passenger cars sales are growing while commercial vehicle sales are shrinking
items.summary: While the industry celebrates total industry volume (TIV) comfortably clearing the 600,000- unit mark during the first nine months, growing four per cent year-on-year, a worrying trend is developing in the commercial vehicle market, it is shrinking. Passenger vehicle sales rose sharply by 22 per cent year-on-year in September while commercial vehicle sales contracted by seven per cent for the month, dragging year-to-date performance down by a staggering 13 per cent to just 37,714 units. July's high jump of 30 per cent sales of pick-up trucks was fuelled by the announcement of Budi Diesel subsidy scheme.

items.title: Chery shifts global expansion into high gear
items.summary: WUHU, China: Chery Automobile Co Ltd is shifting gears in its global expansion strategy, with locally manufactured vehicles set to account for more than half of overseas sales next year. Zhang said Chery planned to establish 26 local R&D centres, building on 16 already in operation, to develop products suited to different markets. EXPORTS DRIVE GROWTH Zhang said Chery's annual sales had doubled from about one million vehicles to two million within two years, while the company accounted for one in every four vehicles exported from China.

items.title: Zahid denies sabotaging Madani government over Sabah, Sarawak projects [WATCH]
items.summary: JASIN: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied allegations that he attempted to sabotage the Madani government over the status of rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak. Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, maintained that his remarks on the suspension or cancellation of letters of acceptance for the projects were factual. Rayer described the remarks as an attempt to sabotage the MADANI Government.

items.title: Mount Kinabalu training centre faces calls to halt work over indigenous, environmental concerns
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 3 — The ongoing construction of a high-altitude training centre on Mount Kinabalu has come under scrutiny, with indigenous groups and tourism stakeholders questioning its environmental impact, approvals and whether communities with customary ties to the mountain were adequately consulted. Bundu Tuhan Village Heritage and Culture head Adrian Soros also questioned whether communities with customary ties to the mountain had been consulted, saying many villagers were unaware of the construction. He said the project had obtained approval from the Sabah Parks Board of Trustees and endorsement from the Mount Kinabalu Native Customary Advisory Council.

items.title: Zahid denies trying to sabotage govt, says he has documents on cancelled rural projects
items.summary: JASIN, Nov 3 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied allegations that he intended to sabotage the Madani Government by revealing the cancellation or postponement of rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, maintained that his remarks concerning the suspension or cancellation of Letters of Acceptance (SSTs) for the projects were factual, adding that he was prepared to produce official documents to substantiate his claims. Yesterday, Jelutong MP RSN Rayer, while interjecting during a debate in the Dewan Rakyat, questioned Ahmad Zahid’s statement concerning the cancellation of rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak.

items.title: KL steps up drainage checks ahead of rainy season to prevent flash floods, says Hannah Yeoh
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 3 — Spot checks on drainage systems and cleaning works in Kuala Lumpur are being stepped up to keep drains clear and reduce the risk of flash floods, especially during the rainy season. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said these checks must be carried out thoroughly, including during the dry season, to ensure cleaning works are done properly and drainage systems function well. Hannah said each parliamentary branch office has also activated teams to conduct patrols and channel the latest reports on flash flood-prone areas to the Kuala Lumpur mayor.

items.title: MCMC opens probe into Facebook post allegedly insulting Sultan of Selangor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has reportedly opened an investigation into a Facebook post suspected of containing highly offensive remarks against the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah. According to Bernama , MCMC said in a statement today that the post was also suspected of touching on sensitivities involving race, religion and royalty (3R). MCMC said it viewed seriously the spread of online content suspected of containing false information or insults against the royal institution, particularly material that could undermine social harmony.

items.title: Flood-hit Selangor districts back in firing line as MetMalaysia warns of torrential evening rain across 10 states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an evening thunderstorm warning across large swathes of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak until 8.00pm today, a day after torrential downpours triggered widespread flash floods across the Klang Valley. Perak faces widespread disruption spanning 12 districts, including Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Muallim, Batang Padang, Larut Matang, Selama, Kerian, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, and Bagan Datuk. Across Selangor, the advisory covers Hulu Selangor, Sabak Bernam, and Kuala Selangor, alongside Petaling and Klang, two major urban districts where drainage systems were inundated during Monday’s deluge.

items.title: AGC orders further police action in probe into claims Negeri Sembilan MB was forced to sign proclamation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 —The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) has returned investigation papers concerning allegations that Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was forced to sign an Instrument of Proclamation to the police for further action. In a statement today, the AGC said it had reviewed the investigation papers submitted by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) on Oct 30 concerning the incident. “Accordingly, the investigation papers will be returned to the PDRM today for further action,” the AGC said.

items.title: Anwar says MotoGP 2026 success boosts Malaysia’s global motorsports standing and local economy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The success in staging the Petronas Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (MotoGP) 2026 has not only strengthened the country’s reputation as a host of world-class motorsports events, but also serves as a catalyst for local economic activity, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. “The Petronas Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (MotoGP) 2026 once again proves the country’s ability to organise world-class sporting events that not only attract motorsports fans but also bring benefits to the people and the local economy,” he said in a Facebook post today. The three-day Malaysian MotoGP, held at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) from Oct 30-Nov 1, attracted about 196,000 visitors.

items.title: Melaka’s history of frequent chief minister changes should serve as a warning, says Adly Zahari
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 3 (Bernama) -- Melaka’s previous experience of seeing chief ministers replaced within a short period should serve as a lesson to all political parties to ensure the stability of the state administration is maintained after the 16th Melaka State Election, according to former Chief Minister Adly Zahari. The Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman said political and administrative stability in the state should be a priority for all parties, rather than focusing solely on who would lead the state government after the election. Whoever leads, our commitment is to ensure political stability,” he told Bernama.

items.title: TM Nxera says Iskandar Puteri data centre has required approvals, sustainability measures amid Johor residents’ concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — TM Nxera has said its data centre campus in Iskandar Puteri, Johor, is being developed on designated land with the necessary regulatory approvals, following media reports of residents’ concerns over power transmission infrastructure and data centre development in the area. In a statement today, the company said the project complied with the conditions imposed by the relevant authorities. TM Nxera also said the campus had incorporated sustainability measures into its design and obtained provisional GreenRE Platinum certification.

items.title: Cloud seeding carried out in peninsula, Sarawak to mitigate impact of transboundary haze
items.summary: The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) said the operations were conducted by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) in collaboration with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF). It said the operations covered the northern, central and southern regions of Peninsular Malaysia, as well as Sarawak, during the transboundary haze episode. NRES said the government had also activated various preparedness measures, including the National Open Burning Action Plan and the National Haze Action Plan, to prevent and mitigate the effects of haze.

items.title: Melaka PH unveils manifesto with 12 pledges, targets 25 million visitors by 2032
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 3 — Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) has unveiled its ‘Melaka Rumah Kita’ manifesto, outlining three main thrusts and 12 aspirations aimed at improving public welfare, expanding economic opportunities and promoting clean, transparent and efficient governance. Its chairman, Adly Zahari, said the first thrust focused on transforming Melaka into a smart state to improve efficiency, security and quality of life. Also present were Melaka PH deputy chairman Khoo Poay Tiong and acting Melaka PKR state leadership council chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim.

items.title: Human Resources Ministry ready to assist Utusan Malaysia staff facing possible layoffs, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) is ready to assist media personnel and journalists affected by job layoffs through various forms of aid, including the Employment Insurance System (EIS) under the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso). He said that if the layoffs really happen, the ministry will apply and ask the involved companies to submit applications for assistance and review the eligibility of the affected workers under the EIS. He said the ministry also provided several other intervention measures to help affected workers.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan land revenue rises RM60.36m to RM404m as state eyes RM1b target by 2030
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 3 — Negeri Sembilan’s land revenue collection increased by RM60.36 million to RM404.04 million as at Sept 30, compared with RM343.68 million recorded in the corresponding period last year. He said the achievement was also supported by non-tax revenue, which recorded collections of RM256.29 million against a target of RM245.62 million, while tax revenue collection amounted to RM147.74 million against a target of RM166.24 million. “For state land tax collection, the amount recorded as at Sept 30 this year was RM144.18 million, compared with RM143.64 million in the corresponding period last year, representing a surplus of RM534,975.93.

items.title: Anwar urges LHDN to balance technology with human judgement in tax administration
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, Nov 3 — As of Nov 2, about 269,900 taxpayers submitted a total of 2.14 billion e-invoices, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said its implementation is not intended to introduce new taxes or increase the public’s tax burden. Anwar said technological progress must always be guided by human values to ensure that its use benefits society.

items.title: Daim family loses bid to stop police probe into alleged ‘government overthrow’ plot
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The High Court today reportedly struck out a lawsuit by the family of the late former finance minister Tun Daim Zainuddin and two lawyers seeking to halt a police investigation into an alleged plot to overthrow the government. She also found that allegations that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s public remarks had influenced the investigation were speculative and unsupported by facts, the report said. The plaintiffs were Daim’s widow, Toh Puan Na’imah Abdul Khalid, their sons Amir and Amin, and lawyers Amir Zharif Abdullah and Nizamuddin Hamid, who had named Anwar, Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Mohd Khalid Ismail and the government as defendants.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia needs better tech to counter increasingly sophisticated drug smuggling
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The increasingly sophisticated methods used in drug smuggling require more advanced detection technology at the country’s entry points to ensure that syndicate activities do not escape the attention of the authorities, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said reliance on existing scanning machines at airports was no longer sufficient as the technology was developed to detect weapons and explosives, rather than prohibited substances such as drugs concealed using more complex methods. In this regard, he said new analytical facilities were being put in place to enhance drug detection capabilities.

items.title: PM: Expedite RM700m flood projects after repeated flooding in Sungai Buloh area
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH, Nov 3 —Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered work on the Sungai Buloh and Sungai Damansara flood mitigation projects to be expedited following repeated flooding in the area. He said the two projects, costing nearly RM700 million and already approved by the federal government, must proceed without delay to minimise the risk of further flooding. Anwar said he would obtain a progress report on the federal government's flood mitigation projects this Friday, while Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari is expected to present an update on state-level projects at the State Executive Council meeting on the same day.

items.title: Cheras custodial death probe: Family denies lawyers intimidated forensic specialist, demands focus on justice
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The younger brother of Noorizwan Zulkefly has rejected police allegations that the family’s legal team intimidated a hospital forensic specialist, calling on authorities to halt investigations against their lawyers and keep public scrutiny fixed on his brother’s custodial death. “My wife, the three lawyers and two police officers from Bukit Aman were all present at the meeting with the forensic specialist doctor. Recounting the hospital briefing, Nooranis said he attended the consultation alongside his wife, the three lawyers, and two Bukit Aman police officers.

items.title: Muhyiddin seeks to drop sedition charge over alleged Nenggiri campaign remarks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Former Prime Minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin will submit a representation to drop a charge of uttering seditious words during the 2024 Nenggiri state by-election campaign. His lawyer, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, said the defence received a letter from the palace yesterday, after Muhyiddin was granted an audience by Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah. “Without going into the details, Yang Arif, we wish to inform the court that our client was granted an audience by the palace on Oct 26.

items.title: Singapore teen among three fined RM3,500 under Malaysia’s new illegal racing law
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 3 — A 19-year-old Singaporean man was among three individuals fined RM3,500 each under the newly amended law against illegal racing by the Magistrate’s Court here today. The three, Syajahan Alfian Abdullah, 19; Muhammad Daniel Hakim Mohamad Rashid, 24; and Gonzales Mckhovic anak George, 18, pleaded guilty to engaging in illegal racing and riding their motorcycles in a dangerous manner on the Second Link Expressway last month. The Transport Ministry said the amendments to the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333) were intended to enhance road safety, strengthen enforcement and modernise service delivery by the Road Transport Department (JPJ).

items.title: Anwar says he personally sympathises with Shuhaily, but stresses law and due process apply to everyone
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today defended Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail amid the controversy surrounding the police investigation into Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain over alleged assault. Addressing questions in Parliament, Anwar expressed personal sympathy for the Malaysian Checkpoints and Borders Agency chief but said the rule of law must take its course without executive interference. Yes, he had contributions,” Anwar said, adding that professionalism and adherence to the law remained paramount.
